title: Rectification of a homotopy square by mapping-path objects
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets, homotopy fibers and geometric realization as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X,Y,S,T$ be Kan complexes, with maps $r:X\to S$, $q:Y\to T$, $u:X\to Y$, $v:S\to T$ and a specified simplicial homotopy $H:X\times\Delta^1\to T$ from $qu$ to $vr$. Set
$$E_r=X\times_{S,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,S),\qquad E_q=Y\times_{T,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,T).$$
Write $e_r:E_r\to X$, $e_q:E_q\to Y$ for the projections and $R:E_r\to S$, $Q:E_q\to T$ for terminal evaluation. The two maps on the edges $01$ and $12$ given respectively by $H\circ(e_r\times\mathrm{id})$ and by applying $v$ to the universal path of $E_r$ define a map $E_r\times\Lambda^2_1\to T$. It extends to a simplicial map $C:E_r\times\Delta^2\to T$. For every such extension, its $02$ edge $c$ defines a simplicial map $U=(u e_r,c):E_r\to E_q$ satisfying
$$e_qU=ue_r,\qquad QU=vR.$$
For each vertex $s\in S$ its restriction $R^{-1}(s)\to Q^{-1}(v(s))$ is a model of the homotopy-fiber map for the specified homotopy $H$: at $(x,\gamma)$ its path is the coherent composite of $H_x$ with $v\gamma$, witnessed by $C$. If $C_0,C_1$ are two extensions of this same horn map, there is a simplicial homotopy between them relative to $E_r\times\Lambda^2_1$; its $02$ edge gives a homotopy between $U_0,U_1$ for which the projection to $Y$ is constantly $ue_r$ and the projection to $T$ is constantly $vR$. In particular it restricts on every strict fiber to a homotopy of the fiber maps. For a vertex $(x,\gamma)$, the realized path $c_{(x,\gamma)}$ is homotopic relative to endpoints to the concatenation $|H_x|\cdot|v\gamma|$. No weak-equivalence hypothesis on $u$ or $v$, and no fibration hypothesis on $r$ or $q$, is imposed; empty complexes and fibers are permitted.

source.place: Corollaries 2.3.2.2 and 2.3.2.4, printed pp. 100-101 (PDF pp. 117-118): parameterized coherent composition and its relative uniqueness. Agent-formulated application to mapping-path objects; not an assertion that HTT states this square verbatim. Online source read; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial comparison.

proof.text: Put $A=E_r$ and write $\Gamma:A\times\Delta^1\to S$ for evaluation of its path coordinate. The pullback condition gives $\Gamma|_0=re_r$ and $\Gamma|_1=R$. On $A\times[0,1]$ prescribe $H(e_r,-)$, and on $A\times[1,2]$ prescribe $v\Gamma$, identifying each displayed edge with $\Delta^1$ in increasing order. Their restrictions to the common vertex $1$ are both $vre_r$. The horn $\Lambda^2_1$ is the union of exactly these edges, so these prescriptions agree on the intersection in every degree and give a simplicial map $h:A\times\Lambda^2_1\to T$ by degreewise gluing.

source.place: Agent application: definition of the horn map; internal evaluation and degreewise gluing.

proof.text: Use the lifting-property convention of [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. The inclusion $i:\Lambda^2_1\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$ is inner anodyne directly: every inner fibration has the right lifting property against this particular inner horn, so $i$ has the required left lifting property. Apply the cited pushout-product theorem to $i$ and the degreewise injective map $\varnothing\to A$. Up to switching the product factors its resulting map is $k:A\times\Lambda^2_1\hookrightarrow A\times\Delta^2$, so $k$ is inner anodyne. Since $T$ is Kan, $T\to\Delta^0$ lifts every inner horn and is an inner fibration. Its lifting property against $k$ extends $h$ to $C:A\times\Delta^2\to T$. The argument does not require $A$ to be Kan or nonempty.

source.place: Lines 103-109 (SSet.innerAnodyneExtensions_pushoutObjObjι'); definitions at Inner/Basic.lean:39-43 and Quasicategory/InnerFibration.lean:61-64; application with empty source in the second factor.

proof.text: Let $c:A\times\Delta^1\to T$ be restriction of $C$ to its edge $02$. Its endpoints are $que_r$ and $vR$, because all three vertices lie in the prescribed horn. The internal functor definition gives a simplicial map $\widehat c:A\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,T)$: on $a:\Delta^n\to A$ it is the map $(t,z)\mapsto c(a(z),t)$ on $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$. This formula commutes with precomposition by every simplicial operator. Its initial evaluation is $que_r$; hence the pair $(ue_r,\widehat c)$ lies in the degreewise pullback $E_q$. This constructs $U$, and the two coordinate evaluations give $e_qU=ue_r$ and $QU=vR$.

source.place: Agent application: adjunction by the explicit internal-functor formula and pullback equations.

proof.text: For a vertex $s\in S$, the definition of homotopy fiber in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] identifies $R^{-1}(s)$ with the model consisting of $(x,\gamma)$ with $\gamma(0)=r(x)$ and $\gamma(1)=s$, including all higher simplices of these data. Likewise $Q^{-1}(v(s))$ is the specified model for $q$ at $v(s)$. The equation $QU=vR$ restricts $U$ to these models. Its formula is $(x,\gamma)\mapsto(u(x),c_{(x,\gamma)})$. Restricting $C$ to this parameter gives a triangle with successive edges $H_x$, $v\gamma$ and long edge $c_{(x,\gamma)}$. Thus this is exactly the coherently composed-path model of the fiber map for $H$, with the triangle giving its composition witness in every simplicial degree.

source.place: Agent application: homotopy-fiber definition and the constructed triangle.

proof.text: For two fillers $C_0,C_1$, put $B=A\times\Delta^2$ and $K=A\times\Lambda^2_1$. Step 2 proved $k:K\hookrightarrow B$ inner anodyne. The map $j:\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is degreewise injective. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] to $k,j$: the inclusion $D=(K\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{K\times\partial\Delta^1}(B\times\partial\Delta^1)\hookrightarrow B\times\Delta^1$ is inner anodyne. Define $D\to T$ by $C_0$ on $B\times\{0\}$, $C_1$ on $B\times\{1\}$, and $h\operatorname{pr}_K$ on $K\times\Delta^1$. These maps agree on each overlap because both fillers restrict to $h$. Lifting against the inner fibration $T\to\Delta^0$ gives $F:B\times\Delta^1\to T$. It restricts to $C_0,C_1$ at the homotopy endpoints and is constant in that coordinate on $K$. This is the required simplicial homotopy relative to the entire horn.

source.place: Lines 103-109; application to the inner-anodyne map of step 2 and the boundary monomorphism of the homotopy interval.

proof.text: Restrict $F$ to $A\times[0,2]\times\Delta^1$, and call the resulting path family $f$. Its path endpoints are $que_r\operatorname{pr}_A$ and $vR\operatorname{pr}_A$, independent of the homotopy coordinate, since the vertices $0,2$ belong to the horn on which $F$ is fixed. The same internal-functor formula as in step 3 therefore pairs $f$ with $ue_r\operatorname{pr}_A$ to give $\mathcal U:A\times\Delta^1\to E_q$. It has endpoint maps $U_0,U_1$, projection to $Y$ equal to $ue_r\operatorname{pr}_A$, and projection under $Q$ equal to $vR\operatorname{pr}_A$. Restricting its $A$ coordinate to $R^{-1}(s)$ consequently lands in $Q^{-1}(v(s))$ for the whole homotopy, proving the claimed fiberwise independence.

source.place: Agent application: restriction of the relative homotopy and its endpoint equations.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $a=(x,\gamma)\in A$. The simplex $C_a$ gives the continuous characteristic map $\sigma:|\Delta^2|\to|T|$, namely $w\mapsto[C_a,w]$ in the realization quotient. Let $e_0,e_1,e_2$ be the three standard vertices and set $d(t)=(1-t)e_0+te_2$. Set $b(t)=(1-2t)e_0+2te_1$ for $0\leq t\leq1/2$, and $b(t)=(2-2t)e_1+(2t-1)e_2$ for $1/2\leq t\leq1$. The two formulas agree at $1/2$, so $b$ is continuous. The convex interpolation $(t,z)\mapsto\sigma((1-z)d(t)+zb(t))$ stays in the triangle and fixes its endpoints for every $z$. At $z=0$ it is the realized $02$ edge; at $z=1$ it traverses the $01$ and $12$ edges in succession, which are $|H_x|$ and $|v\gamma|$ by the quotient relation for faces. This is the asserted endpoint-relative path homotopy. All constructions above are conditional only on the displayed data: if $A$ or a strict fiber is empty its restrictions are unique, while a vertex $a$ is chosen only for this last assertion. No equivalence condition on $u,v$ or fibration condition on $r,q$ was used.

source.place: Agent application: explicit convex interpolation in the characteristic two-simplex.
